title: Diary of a CEO: Huberman's 10 daily protocols from Protocols
summary: Huberman walks through ten daily practices in sequence: hydration, morning light, early exercise, cold exposure, physiological sighs, evening light, a dark sleep environment, focused learning, and personal development. The through-line is a high morning cortisol peak that sets up low cortisol and good sleep at night. He also covers a short supplement stack, walking after meals, and his views on peptides and prayer.

principles.text: Aim for a high cortisol peak early in the day; it sets up low cortisol and better sleep at night.
principles.quote: You want this peak in cortisol as high as possible in the first 60 minutes of your day.

principles.text: Get daylight in your eyes early in the day, outdoors rather than through glass; use a 10,000 lux light if there is no sun.
principles.quote: But you want daylight in your eyes in the first hours of your day. Go out on your balcony if that's all you can do.

principles.text: Get some daylight in the late afternoon or evening to buffer the effects of artificial light at night.
principles.quote: try and get some daylight in your eyes in the late afternoon or evening if you're going to be working indoors from after lunch until nightfall.

principles.text: Exercise in the first few hours of the day when you can; it gives a useful cortisol inflection and entrains your schedule.
principles.quote: there's a huge advantage to doing cardiovascular resistance training in the first 3 hours of your day.

principles.text: Use the physiological sigh (double inhale, long exhale) to cut stress in real time.
principles.quote: you just breathe until your lungs are empty, and it's immediate.

principles.text: Learning requires effortful attempts with errors; the errors drive plasticity, followed by self-testing.
principles.quote: The error is what stimulates the plasticity.
